title: Evaluating sin^2(3*pi/8) via the Half-Angle Formula
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use a half-angle identity to find the exact value of \sin^2(3\pi/8).

steps.title: Apply the Half-Angle Identity for Sine Squared
steps.explanation: Set theta = 3*pi/8 in sin^2(theta) = (1 - cos(2*theta))/2 so that 2*theta = 3*pi/4.
steps.why: Doubling 3*pi/8 gives the Quadrant II special angle 3*pi/4.

steps.title: Evaluate cos(3*pi/4)
steps.explanation: In Quadrant II, 3*pi/4 has reference angle pi/4 and negative cosine.

steps.title: Simplify the Expression
steps.explanation: Substitute -sqrt(2)/2 and multiply numerator and denominator by 2.
steps.why: Subtracting a negative adds +sqrt(2)/2, and multiplying by 2/2 yields (2 + sqrt(2))/4.
